title: Omega Announces Its Planned Leadership Transition
summary: Taylor Pickett, CEO, to retire October 1st; stepping down from Board of Directors Matthew Gourmand, President, promoted to CEO; to join…...
body_text: Omega Announces Its Planned Leadership Transition May 21, 2026 4:15pm EDT Download as PDF Taylor Pickett, CEO, to retire October 1st; stepping down from Board of Directors Matthew Gourmand, President, promoted to CEO; to join Board Bob Stephenson, CFO, to retire August 1st Neal Ballew, CAO, promoted to CFO HUNT VALLEY, Md.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Omega Healthcare Investors, Inc. (NYSE: OHI) (the “Company” or “Omega”) today announced that Matthew Gourmand, President of Omega, will become the Company’s Chief Executive Officer in conjunction with the planned retirement of Taylor Pickett effective October 1, 2026. Mr. Pickett will step down from the Board of Directors upon his retirement, and the Board of Directors intends to appoint Mr. Gourmand to the Board, effective on that date. Omega also announced the planned retirement of Bob Stephenson as the Company’s Chief Financial Officer effective August 1, 2026, with Neal Ballew, currently Omega’s Chief Accounting Officer of six years, succeeding Mr. Stephenson in that role. Craig Callen, Chair of the Board of Directors, stated, “I am excited to announce the next generation leadership of Omega, with Matthew and Neal stepping up into the CEO and CFO roles as the culmination of a carefully managed, multi-year succession plan. The Board has been developing this plan over an extended period and believes it will lead to Omega’s continued success.” Mr. Callen continued regarding Mr. Gourmand, “We have had the opportunity to see Matthew evolve in various roles and, with his deep investing experience and a leadership style rooted in collaboration and innovation, he is well-prepared to lead the Company in its next phase of growth.” Mr. Pickett stated, “Having worked with Matthew for the past eight years, I believe he is the right person to take the Company forward. With a highly experienced and driven team to support him, I am confident that Omega is well-positioned to continue to increase shareholder value.” Mr. Pickett’s retirement marks the end of a remarkable 25 years as Omega’s CEO, during which Omega has achieved a total shareholder return of over 10,000%, the highest return of all publicly traded REITs over that period. Its portfolio of predominantly senior care assets grew from 258 to 1,124 as of the past quarter, and its market capitalization increased from approximately $60 million to over $15 billion today. Mr. Callen commented, “Throughout Taylor’s 25 years as CEO of Omega, his strategic vision and strong leadership have created an industry-leading company well-positioned to capture current and future demographic trends. Taylor created a strong culture based on achievement, prudent capital allocation and development of future executives. That team now stands ready to build upon this success.” Mr. Stephenson also has had a remarkable career at Omega, overseeing significant growth in the capital base and the establishment of investment grade credit ratings, reflecting strong balance sheet management. Mr. Pickett stated, “During Bob’s 25-year tenure as CFO, his financial management has been exceptional. He inherited a deeply challenged balance sheet, which he has methodically and judiciously strengthened over the years. He leaves Omega as an investment-grade credit, with a well-laddered maturity schedule, and leverage near all-time lows, with Neal very well-trained and ready to step up. I would like to thank Bob for being such a great partner to me in the leadership of Omega.” Mr. Callen continued, “We thank both Taylor and Bob for their unwavering service to shareholders and wish each of them a long and well-deserved retirement.” Mr. Pickett said, “It has been an honor and a privilege to lead Omega since 2001. I am proud of our team’s many accomplishments, and I am grateful to my colleagues, our Board of Directors, our operating partners, and all those who have contributed to Omega’s success during my tenure.” Mr. Stephenson commented, “It has been the highlight of my professional life to be part of the Omega leadership team and oversee the financial evolution and growth of the Company from its early day struggles to its present position as a large scale, financially sound industry leader.” Mr. Stephenson continued, “I have worked very closely with Neal since he joined Omega. He is highly skilled, bright, and talented, and will provide great continuity. As we start a multi-decade tailwind from the aging of the baby boomers, and with Matthew and Neal ready to step into their new roles, I feel as confident about the future of Omega as I feel proud of the past.” Reflecting on his impending new role, Mr. Gourmand noted, “I am excited to serve as Omega’s next CEO and lead this exceptional team in its next chapter. I am grateful for the trust that the Board has placed in me, and I will work tirelessly to repay that trust. I want to thank Taylor and Bob for growing and shaping Omega into what it is today, as well as all their mentorship and counsel to prepare me for this next step. They will be deeply missed, but the culture of excellence and an unwavering focus on creating shareholder value will continue.” Both Mr. Pickett and Mr. Stephenson have agreed to remain in consulting roles after their retirements, being available to the Company as requested from time to time during their consulting periods. Omega is a real estate investment trust (“REIT”) that invests in the long-term healthcare industry, primarily in skilled nursing and assisted living facilities. Its portfolio of assets is operated by a diverse group of healthcare companies, predominantly in a triple-net lease structure. The assets span all regions within the U.S., as well as in the U.K. Forward-Looking Statements and Cautionary Language This press release includes forward-looking statements within the meaning of the federal securities laws. (vii) the availability and cost of capital to Omega; (viii) changes in Omega’s credit ratings and the ratings of its debt securities; (ix) competition in the financing of healthcare facilities; (x) competition in the long-term healthcare industry and shifts in the perception of various types of long-term care facilities, including SNFs and ALFs; (xi) changes in the financial position of Omega’s operators; (xii) the effect of economic, regulatory and market conditions generally, and particularly in the healthcare industry in the U.S. and in other jurisdictions where we conduct business, including the U.K.; (xiii) changes in interest rates and foreign currency exchange rates and the impact of inflation and changes in global tariffs and international trade disputes; (xiv) the timing, amount and yield of any additional investments; (xv) Omega’s ability to maintain its status as a REIT; (xvi) operational risks associated with our investments in healthcare operating companies, including senior housing properties managed through structures authorized by the REIT Investment Diversification and Empowerment Act of 2007 (commonly referred to as “RIDEA”); (xvii) the use of, or inability to use, artificial intelligence by us, our operators, managers, vendors and investors; (xviii) the effect of other factors affecting our business or the businesses of Omega’s operators that are beyond Omega’s or operators’ control, including natural disasters, public health crises or pandemics, cyber threats and governmental action, particularly in the healthcare industry, and (xix) other factors identified in Omega’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. 2026 Women of H&P Awardees Announced
summary: H&P has announced the recipients of the Women of H&P Awards, recognizing employees for leadership, professional growth and contributions across the organization. The awards honor women who demonstrate H&P’s values through their work and influence. Employees across the company were nominated by their peers, reflecting a broad range of impact and achievement. Discover more at H&P
body_text: 2026 Women of H&P Awardees Announced H&P has announced the recipients of the Women of H&P Awards, recognizing employees for leadership, professional growth and contributions across the organization. The awards honor women who demonstrate H&P’s values through their work and influence. Employees across the company were nominated by their peers, reflecting a broad range of impact and achievement. Samiya Sleem Shahbal honored with Woman of the Year Woman of H&P Award Samiya Sleem Shahbal, a document controller with the E&M team based in the Muscat office, has been named a Woman of H&P Award winner in the Woman of the Year category, recognizing her quiet dedication, teamwork and behind-the-scenes contributions during 18 years of service at H&P. Shahbal supports operations by working closely with PDO rigs to upload documentation directly into the eCCC (Electronic Check, Comply and Confirm) system. She also manages timesheets for the E&M department, including both office staff and rig-based supervisors—work that requires consistency, attention to detail and strong coordination across teams. “To me, this award represents the trust and appreciation of my team,” Shahbal said. “It reminds me that even small, consistent efforts — helping colleagues, staying positive and putting the team first — can make a meaningful impact.” Her pride in her work is closely tied to the success of those around her. Rather than a single defining moment, Shahbal said her proudest professional experiences have come from watching her team perform under pressure. “Seeing the team succeed, stay strong and achieve our goals despite the pressure made me truly proud,” she said. “It wasn’t just about the results, but the collaboration, trust and resilience we built along the way.” Throughout her career, Shahbal has navigated demanding workloads and high-pressure situations. She credits organization, clear communication and a positive mindset for helping her overcome those challenges. “With the support of my team, I was able to handle difficult situations successfully and grow stronger and more resilient,” she said. The Woman of the Year award reflects Shahbal’s willingness to step in and support others without expecting recognition. During particularly busy periods, she said, she has frequently taken on additional tasks to help colleagues manage heavy workloads and meet deadlines. “I didn’t do it for recognition,” she said. “I did it to help and support others.” That mindset defines how Shahbal views teamwork. “Being a team player means helping others, working together and always putting the team first,” she said. She credits her professional growth to the influence of a mentor who guided her with patience and integrity. “Their encouragement helped me build confidence, stay grounded and focus on teamwork and continuous growth,” Shahbal said. Integrity, humility and teamwork are the values that guide her work each day. She believes in doing the right thing, staying grounded and supporting those around her—even when the work happens quietly behind the scenes. “I’m motivated by knowing my work helps the team succeed, even if it’s not always seen,” she said. “I take pride in supporting others and growing every day.” Looking ahead, Shahbal hopes to continue learning, developing her skills and taking on greater responsibilities while staying true to the values that have shaped her career. Outside of work, she enjoys reading, walking and spending time with her family. She describes herself as caring, loving and friendly—“but with limits,” she added with a smile. Shahbal offered her thanks to the entire Oman team for their continued support and encouragement. “I’m grateful to work here and with the best colleagues,” she said. For women entering the industry, her advice is simple and heartfelt: believe in yourself, keep learning, speak up, seek mentors and support other women. “Be resilient,” she said. “You belong here, and you can make a real impact.” Kathryn Watson Named Women of H&P Humble Heroine Award Winner Kathryn Watson, an intelligence analyst with H&P’s Global Security team, has been named the recipient of the Women of H&P Award in the Humble Heroine category, recognizing her behind-the-scenes contributions and unwavering commitment to team success. Watson, who is based in Houston, has spent the past six years at H&P helping safeguard the company’s people and assets around the world. As part of Global Security, she analyzes large volumes of information to identify potential risks that could impact operations in diverse and often complex environments. “The Global Security team’s goal is to enable business in any environment,” Watson said. “My role is to sort through all the varied information coming in and figure out what is truly a potential risk that could affect our people and assets.” Despite the individual recognition, Watson emphasized that the award reflects a collective effort rather than personal achievement. “I am so fortunate to work with a fantastic team,” she said. “Any recognition that comes my way is really a reflection of a team effort that I am part of.” Watson said she is especially proud to work for a company that prioritizes employee well-being, pointing to H&P’s ongoing support for employees and their families during the conflict in the Middle East. Her path to becoming an intelligence analyst was shaped by hands-on operational experience in both the U.S. Navy and the energy industry. Watson served aboard Navy ships, learning engineering, weapons systems and navigation, before transitioning to the energy sector through Shell’s Supervisor in Training program, where she began her career on the rig. “Each time it felt daunting,” she said. “But I had great mentors who took the time to really teach me how things worked. Understanding how operations work has made me a better intelligence analyst.” Among those mentors, Watson credits Mark Nagle, a former Shell drilling superintendent, for helping her see long-term potential in the industry. At H&P, she expressed gratitude to her manager, Rob Ream, for his guidance and support, as well as to colleagues in the Houston office “for always keeping it fun.” The Humble Heroine award recognizes employees who consistently support their teams without seeking recognition. Watson’s nomination highlighted her inclusive approach to collaboration, particularly her efforts to accommodate colleagues working across multiple time zones. “That’s not above and beyond,” Watson said. “It’s just trying to be inclusive.” Guided by a service-oriented mindset, Watson defines strong teamwork as a shared understanding of the mission and how each role contributes to it. Looking ahead, she said she is excited to support H&P’s continued global expansion. For the next generation of women entering the industry, her advice is simple: “Stay curious and never stop learning.” Outside of work, Watson enjoys reading, running and traveling, as well as spending time with her partner, George, and their beagle, Murphy. She is also a self-proclaimed crossword puzzle aficionado — a fitting hobby for someone who describes herself in three words as “seeking to understand.” Chelsey Robinson honored with Woman of H&P Award for Lifelong Learning Chelsey Robinson, a contracts coordinator II based in Tulsa, has been named a Woman of H&P Award winner in the Lifelong Learner category, recognizing her dedication to continuous growth, adaptability and team-driven excellence during her 13-year career at H&P. Robinson supports the contracts team alongside LaRae Levy, April Rodrigues, Storri Wild, Allison Astor, Tiffany Haddock and Aditya Pilgaokar. In her role, she drafts, formats, reviews and organizes contracts, amendments and related documents while ensuring each aligns with company policies and legal standards. “Being acknowledged is incredibly motivating, and it inspires me to continue striving for excellence,” Robinson said. “It’s meaningful to know the work I do adds value.” Robinson’s path at H&P reflects the spirit of the Lifelong Learner award. After spending 10 years in one department, she made the decision to step into a new role within the company — a challenge that required confidence, adaptability and a willingness to learn. “Stepping outside my comfort zone was difficult, but it pushed me to grow both professionally and personally,” she said. “It turned out to be one of the best decisions I’ve made.” That growth mindset continues to define her work today. Robinson said she actively seeks opportunities to strengthen her skills, most recently focusing on the “letter side” of contracts — reviewing and understanding contract language, analyzing prior correspondence and ensuring accuracy across documentation that directly impacts day-to-day operations. “There is always something new to learn in the contracts world,” she said. “I genuinely appreciate feedback from leaders and coworkers and view it as guidance rather than criticism.” Her approach to learning extends beyond the workplace. As a mother of three boys heavily involved in sports, Robinson said organization and balance are essential — and humor helps, too. “Staying organized is less of a skill and more of a survival tactic,” she said with a laugh. “I also try to keep up with today’s slang so I can maintain my status as the ‘cool mom.’” Robinson credits her values — integrity, respect, accountability and teamwork — as the foundation of her success. She strives to bring a positive attitude to work each day, remain open to learning and support her teammates. “The people around me make a huge difference,” she said. “We genuinely feel like family.” She offered special thanks to the entire Contracts team, along with several colleagues across the organization who have supported her growth. She also gave a heartfelt shoutout to Kate Foltz, whom she described as “the best friend and best co-worker anyone could ask for.” Outside of H&P, Robinson enjoys spending time with her husband and cheering on her sons at baseball and football games. She describes herself as loyal, organized and positive — traits that clearly resonate in her professional journey. Looking ahead, Robinson hopes to continue growing within the Contracts department while learning alongside the team she’s proud to be part of. For the next generation of women entering the industry, her advice is simple: “Step out of your comfort zone and give yourself permission to grow. If you’re struggling, don’t hold it in. Being open and vulnerable builds strength, confidence and stronger connections.” True to the Lifelong Learner title, Robinson views growth as an ongoing journey — one fueled by dedication, feedback and a genuine curiosity to keep getting better. AL Anood Ahmed Al Aisri named Woman of H&P Award winner in Leading Lady category AL Anood Ahmed Al Aisri, a technical assistant with the HSSEQT team in Muscat, has been named a Woman of H&P Award winner in the Leading Lady category, recognizing her steady leadership, commitment to safety and positive influence across H&P during more than 12 years of service. Al Aisri has worked at H&P for 12 years and five months and currently serves as an HSE technical assistant and IVMS/DFMS focal point. In her role, she supports the HSE team by maintaining accurate safety data and reports, assisting with audits and compliance records, and monitoring driver behavior to identify trends that improve road safety. “I simply do my best to contribute to stronger safety performance through accurate information, steady monitoring and clear communication,” Al Aisri said. Receiving the Leading Lady award, she said, is both meaningful and motivating. “This award means a lot to me,” she said. “It reminds me that my efforts to support safety performance are valued, and it motivates me to keep improving and contributing to the team.” Al Aisri’s career at H&P reflects persistence, adaptability and a willingness to embrace change. She has successfully transitioned through several roles, including positions in marketing and sales, construction HSE and as an LSF secretary, before stepping into her current role. Each move required new skills and rapid learning. “Each step was challenging, but I overcame it by staying committed to learning, seeking guidance and embracing every opportunity to grow,” she said. Her proudest professional moments, Al Aisri said, are not tied to a single event, but to seeing consistent improvements in IVMS and DFMS reporting and the resulting positive impact on road safety performance. “The gradual improvement and appreciation from the team made me feel proud and grateful to contribute to H&P’s safety goals,” she said. As a leader, Al Aisri says her approach is rooted in humility, consistency and teamwork. She believes strong leadership begins with listening and supporting others. “I try to lead by example, stay supportive and focus on clear communication,” she said. “Supporting others consistently matters more than having all the answers.” Those values are reflected in the principles that guide her work daily: accuracy, accountability and teamwork. “I believe in doing my work with integrity, supporting others when needed and always aiming to improve safety and overall performance,” she said. Al Aisri credits her growth to the people around her, particularly her manager and colleagues. “Their support, guidance and encouragement have helped me grow and gain confidence at every step,” she said. “I’m truly grateful for everything they have taught me and for always believing in me.” Being recognized as a woman in a leadership role within the industry carries special meaning for Al Aisri. She said it demonstrates how dedication and trust can open doors for women across H&P. “It shows that dedication can make a difference,” she said. “I’m grateful for the opportunity to contribute, represent other women and support a more inclusive and safer workplace.” Looking ahead, Al Aisri hopes to continue building her skills within HSE, taking on additional responsibilities and contributing to even stronger safety performance. Outside of work, she enjoys spending time with her family, relaxing and camping whenever possible. She describes herself as strong, confident and caring — traits that have helped define her leadership style and professional journey. To the next generation of women entering the industry, Al Aisri offers this advice: “Believe in yourself, stay patient and don’t be afraid to learn new things. Every small step matters, and your voice adds value.” Fatina Al Balushi named Woman of H&P Award winner in Rising Rookie category Fatina Al Balushi, a QA/QC assistant with the HSSEQ team in Oman, has been named a Woman of H&P Award winner in the Rising Rookie category, recognizing her strong early-career contributions, commitment to quality and continuous growth during her first three years at H&P. In her role, Al Balushi supports the quality function by helping ensure compliance with internal processes, documentation standards and customer requirements. She plays a key role in preparing for API and ISO audits by gathering evidence, organizing documentation and verifying that both suppliers and internal operations conform to required standards. “My work focuses on accuracy, consistency and continuous improvement,” Al Balushi said. “The goal is always to help maintain a strong quality culture within the organization.” Receiving the Rising Rookie award, she said, is both meaningful and motivating. “It’s very encouraging to know that my work is recognized and appreciated,” she said. “This acknowledgment motivates me to continue learning, improving and giving my best each day.” Al Balushi said her proudest professional moments have come from watching her own growth since joining H&P. From improving documentation accuracy to supporting audits and identifying potential issues before they escalate, she said each milestone reinforces her confidence and dedication to quality. “Seeing how much I’ve grown and how my work contributes to quality improvements makes me proud,” she said. Starting her career in QA/QC came with challenges, particularly learning complex systems, documentation requirements and audit standards such as API and ISO with limited prior experience. She credits perseverance, curiosity and strong team support for helping her overcome those early hurdles. “I overcame these challenges by asking questions, seeking guidance and continuously improving my technical skills,” she said. “With time, practice and support from the team, I became more confident and capable.” Al Balushi recognizes QA/QC Coordinator Nasser Al Sharii as a key influence on her professional development. “Since my first day at H&P, his guidance, support and trust have played a major role in shaping my growth,” she said. “He encouraged me to take on new challenges, build my skills and develop confidence in my work.” Integrity, responsibility and continuous improvement guide Al Balushi’s work every day. She said she strives to approach each task with honesty, accuracy and a mindset focused on getting better. Drawn to H&P by its critical role in safe and reliable operations, Al Balushi said she has been surprised by how quickly she gained responsibility and hands-on experience early in her career. “I’ve learned that attention to detail, teamwork and adaptability are just as important as technical knowledge,” she said. Looking ahead, Al Balushi hopes to continue developing her QA/QC expertise, expand her understanding of industry standards and take on greater responsibility while contributing to long-term improvement efforts. Outside of work, she enjoys traveling, camping and spending quality time with family and close friends. She describes herself as friendly, confident and creative. Al Balushi expressed appreciation for the support she has received at H&P, offering thanks to her manager and HSSEQ team for their guidance and encouragement. For women entering the industry, her advice is straightforward: “Be confident, stay curious and don’t hesitate to speak up and learn.” As a Rising Rookie, Al Balushi’s dedication, growth mindset and commitment to quality signal a promising future and a lasting impact at H&P. title: Cosmic Rundown: Anthropic Acquires Stainless, Files.md Ships, Linux Security Drowns in AI
summary: Anthropic acquires Stainless for better SDKs, Files.md offers an open-source Obsidian alternative, and AI bug hunters are overwhelming the Linux kernel security team.
body_text: Anthropic Acquires Stainless Anthropic announced it has acquired Stainless , the company behind high-quality SDK generation tooling. Stainless has been quietly powering the official SDKs for OpenAI, Cloudflare, and others. The acquisition signals Anthropic's commitment to developer experience. Good SDKs are the difference between a painful integration and one that just works. Stainless built a reputation for generating TypeScript, Python, and Go clients that feel hand-written rather than auto-generated. For teams building on Claude's API, this likely means continued improvement in SDK quality. For the broader ecosystem, it raises questions about whether Stainless will continue supporting non-Anthropic clients. Files.md: An Open-Source Obsidian Alternative A new project called Files.md hit the front page. It's positioning itself as an open-source alternative to Obsidian, built around plain markdown files. The pitch is simple: your notes are just files. No proprietary format, no sync lock-in, no plugin ecosystem you have to buy into. The project is early but the approach resonates with developers who want their knowledge management system to be as portable as a git repository. Whether it gains traction depends on execution. Obsidian's strength isn't just the file format. It's the graph view, the plugin system, and years of polish. But for developers who want something lighter and more hackable, Files.md is worth watching. Linux Security Mailing List Overwhelmed by AI Bug Hunters Linus Torvalds and the kernel security team are dealing with an unexpected problem: AI-powered bug hunters have made the Linux security mailing list almost unmanageable . The issue is volume. AI tools can scan codebases and generate security reports at scale. But many of these reports are low-quality, duplicative, or false positives. The kernel team now spends significant time triaging submissions that a human researcher would have filtered before sending. This is a pattern we'll see more of. AI lowers the barrier to participation in security research, but it doesn't automatically raise the quality. The result is maintainer burnout and signal-to-noise problems that open-source projects aren't staffed to handle. Other Notable Conversations GenCAD - A generative CAD tool that's generating significant interest. The intersection of AI and mechanical design is heating up. Semble - A code search tool for AI agents that claims 98% fewer tokens than grep. As agent-based development grows, tooling that reduces token costs will become increasingly valuable. Auto-identity-remove - An automated data broker opt-out runner for macOS. Privacy automation is a growing category. Project Glasswing - Cloudflare published findings from Mythos, their work on cyber frontier models. Worth reading if you're thinking about AI and security. What This Means for Content Teams The Stainless acquisition is a reminder that developer experience extends beyond documentation. The SDK is often the first touchpoint a developer has with your API. Investing in that layer pays dividends. The Linux security situation is a preview of what happens when AI tools outpace the systems designed to process their output. If your team accepts automated submissions of any kind, consider whether your processes can handle 10x the volume at potentially lower quality. And if you're evaluating note-taking tools for technical documentation, the Files.md approach of plain files plus git is worth considering. Portability matters when your knowledge base needs to outlast any single vendor.

title: Timken Details Strategy and Announces 2028 Financial Targets at Investor Day

body_text: NORTH CANTON, Ohio , May 20, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- The Timken Company (NYSE: TKR; www.timken.com ), a leader in advanced motion technology, hosted an Investor Day earlier today in New York City. Lucian Boldea, president and CEO, and other members of Timken's executive team detailed the company's 2028 financial targets and strategy to accelerate profitable growth, structurally increase margins and drive value for shareholders. "Today, we introduced our Elevate to Outperform strategy, which is focused on optimizing our portfolio, investing decisively in our strategic verticals, and better leveraging our multinational footprint as we operate as One Timken," said Boldea. "Execution of our plan is well underway to achieve compelling 2028 financial targets and deliver enhanced value to our customers and shareholders over the long term." Highlights from Timken's 2028 financial targets include: Total sales of $5.0 to $5.2 billion, with an organic net sales CAGR percentage in the mid-single digits Industrial Motion segment adjusted EBITDA margin of 25 to 27 percent of sales in 2028, up from 19 percent in 2025 Engineered Bearings segment adjusted EBITDA margin of 21 to 23 percent of sales in 2028, up from 18.9 percent in 2025 Adjusted earnings per share of approximately $8.50, a greater than 55 percent increase compared to 2025 Presentation materials and a replay of the webcast are available at http://investors.timken.com . The webcast passcode is TimkenNYSE and will be accessible until June 3, 2026. About The Timken Company The Timken Company (NYSE: TKR; www.timken.com ), a leader in advanced motion technology, designs and manufacturers highly engineered systems and components for customers in strategic end markets, including aerospace and defense, power and electrification, and automation and industrial solutions. With more than 125 years of specialized expertise and a multinational presence, Timken is a trusted partner worldwide, innovating and powering performance across the application lifecycle. The company posted $4.6 billion in sales in 2025 and employs approximately 19,000 people, operating from 45 countries. Learn more at www.timken.com or @TheTimkenCompany . title: What Are the 2026 Updates to OSHA’s Revised Heat Stress National Emphasis Program (NEP)?
summary: On April 10, 2026, OSHA issued a revised National Emphasis Program (NEP) on Outdoor and Indoor Heat-Related Hazards, replacing the version first issued in 2022. The program is effective immediately and will remain in place for five years.
body_text: Reading Time: 4 minutes On April 10, 2026, OSHA issued a revised National Emphasis Program (NEP) on Outdoor and Indoor Heat-Related Hazards , replacing the version first issued in 2022 . The program is effective immediately and will remain in place for five years.1 Heat-related stress and illness often remain a top concern across a number of industries, particularly during the summer season. In fact, the NEP states that “OSHA’s heat-related inspections have accounted for 6% of all federal-level agency inspections in the past five years. That’s an increase from 0.5% over the five-year period that preceded the 2022 NEP.”2 According to OSHA’s media release announcing the NEP, “Ensuring that employers take the steps needed to safeguard workers is essential, and this updated National Emphasis allows OSHA to better focus its outreach, compliance assistance, and enforcement efforts in high-risk industries and promote effective prevention practices.”3 Although the OSHA heat NEP is not a formal OSHA standard, it helps direct how compliance officers conduct inspections and issue citations related to heat hazards. What is the Goal of the OSHA Heat NEP 2026? The NEP tells OSHA compliance officers when and where to focus enforcement related to heat exposure, and is “intended to encourage early interventions by employers to prevent illnesses and deaths among workers during high heat conditions, such as working outdoors in a local area experiencing a heat wave, as announced by the National Weather Service.”4 It authorizes both programmed inspections (planned inspections in targeted industries) and unprogrammed inspections based on complaints, referrals, hospitalizations, fatalities, or visible heat hazards observed on site.4 Why Did OSHA Revise the Heat NEP? By revising and continuing the Heat NEP, OSHA aims to “ensure that employees in high-hazard industries are protected from heat-related hazards, both indoors and outdoors, that may lead to serious illnesses, injuries, or death.”4 OSHA revised the NEP to help: Update enforcement priorities Clarify inspection procedures Improve consistency in citations Formalize how heat programs are evaluated What are the Key Changes to the OSHA NEP as of April 2026? 1. Updated List of Targeted Industries Compared to the previous Heat NEP issued in 2022, this 2026 update resulted in 46 target industries removed, 22 industries added, and 33 industries retained, for a total of 55 target industries.4 Construction industries identified as being likely to have heat-related hazards include:4 Residential building construction Nonresidential building construction Highway, street, and bridge construction Utility system construction Foundation and building exterior contractors Specialty trade contractors Additional industries listed in the NEP that may be likely to have heat-related hazards include Electric Power Generation, Transmission, and Distribution, and Architectural, Engineering, and Related Services. 2. Removal of the Numerical Inspection Goal The 2022 NEP included a defined goal to increase heat inspections compared to prior years. The revised NEP removes that numerical target. Instead, OSHA now uses: Current injury and illness data Local weather conditions Prior enforcement history This change allows OSHA to “direct agency resources where they can make the biggest impact – focusing inspections and outreach in industries and workplaces where heat stress risks are most likely to occur.”1 3. Continued Random Inspections on Heat Advisory Days The revised NEP confirms that OSHA compliance officers may conduct random inspections in targeted industries on days when the National Weather Service issues a heat advisory or heat warning.4 On these days, officers may: Open a heat-related inspection without a complaint Expand an unrelated inspection if heat hazards are observed Document heat index, humidity, wind, workload, clothing, and rest practices For construction sites, this means heat controls should be in place and functioning whenever elevated temperatures are forecast. What are some additional updates to the OSHA Heat NEP? Additional revisions made to the OSHA Heat NEP as of April 2026 compared to the original version include: Reorganized and Added Appendix I: Evaluation of a Heat Program Reorganized and Added Appendix J: Citation Guidance Added coding for Worksite Assistance Added coding for Unprogrammed Emphasis Hazards Considerations for Safety Managers and Employers The revised NEP does not change the basic elements of heat stress protection, but in light of the updated NEP, safety managers and employers may want to consider: Reviewing heat stress protection plans against Appendix I criteria Making efforts to ensure water, shade, and rest practices are consistently available Documenting acclimatization and daily heat planning Training supervisors to recognize and respond to heat illness Monitoring weather forecasts and prepare for heat advisory days PPE Solutions for Worker Heat Stress In addition, PPE that helps to reduce heat stress may help enhance worker safety in conditions where outdoor heat stress is a concern. Innovative solutions that may be considered include: MSA V-Gard C1® Hard Hat : The patented ReflectIR™ Thermal Barrier technology helps keep the inside of the hard hat up to 20°F cooler in sunny conditions. The moisture-wicking sweat band with breathable foam padding helps provide additional comfort and sweat management, while the larger brim helps provide sun and shade protection. MSA V-Gard® Cooling Pads : Both the Crown cooler and Crown cooler with neck shade (UPF 50+) feature HyperKewl™ evaporative cooling fabric to help provide extended relief from heat fatigue and heat stress. Looking for more safety tips and information to help enhance heat stress compliance? Check out more resources, including Prepare for Seasonal Heat Stress: The OSHA NEP and Tips for Employers , which includes details around the original OSHA Heat NEP issued in April 2022 and extended until April 2026, and What to Consider When Choosing Heat Stress PPE: Design Features and Materials .
